Frequently Asked Questions

Need answers? We’ve got you covered.

Common questions about lodging an Annual Trust Tax Return. Still not sure? Our team is one call away.

Call Us Now
What is an Annual Trust Tax Return?
An Annual Trust Tax Return is a financial report submitted to the ATO outlining the trust’s income, expenses, and distributions.
Who needs to file an Annual Trust Tax Return?
Any trust that earns income or distributes funds to beneficiaries must file an Annual Trust Tax Return.
When is the Annual Trust Tax Return due?
The deadline is typically 31 October each year unless extended by a tax agent.
What happens if I fail to lodge my Annual Trust Tax Return?
Failure to lodge may result in fines, penalties, and increased scrutiny from the ATO
Can I claim deductions on my Annual Trust Tax Return?
Yes, deductions may include property expenses, investment costs, and administrative fees.
Can I prepare my trust tax return without a professional?
Yes, but working with a tax agent ensures accuracy, maximised deductions, and ATO compliance.
How long does it take to lodge an Annual Trust Tax Return?
The process typically takes 2 to 4 weeks, depending on the complexity of your financial data.
Is there a penalty for late lodgement?
Yes, the ATO imposes penalties for late submissions unless valid reasons are provided.
What information do I need to lodge my trust tax return?
You’ll need income statements, expense records, and beneficiary distribution details.
Why should I choose Ideal Business Group?
We offer accurate tax return lodgement, maximise your deductions, and ensure full ATO compliance.
